newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke wrote EMU thank you notes - Treasury.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke wrote EMU thank you notes - Treasury.

text.p: The UK Treasury confirmed on Friday Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke wrote thank you letters to 15 leading industrialists after they wrote a letter to the Financial Times calling for the government to leave open all options on EMU.
But a Treasury spokesman played down the significance of letters, saying they thanked the business leaders for supporting governemnt policy.
"Government policy all along as been to keep the options open (on European monetary union) so the letter thanked them for backing government policy," he said.
The Financial Times published the letter on September 5, and the paper reported on Friday Clarke sent his thank-you notes the next day.

"It is extremely important that people in critical private sector positions such as yourself argue in public for keeping our options firmly open in a single currency," the letters said, according to the FT.

The letter pre-dates the recent internecine row on government policy over European monetary union sparked by comments from Clarke last weekend that it would be "pathetic' for Britain to not make up its mind and then join EMU late.
